qualityAttributes.name: Accessibility
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software is usable by people with disabilities, often through assistive technologies.

qualityAttributes.name: Accountability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software keeps accurate records and has the ability to explain its operations.

qualityAttributes.name: Accuracy
qualityAttributes.definition: The capability of the software to retrieve and rank data accurately according to given specifications.

qualityAttributes.name: Adaptability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software adapts its behavior based on information about its users and environment.

qualityAttributes.name: Administrability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which users with elevated permissions can effectively configure the software.

qualityAttributes.name: Affordability
qualityAttributes.definition: The cost of the software as it relates to what the purchaser can afford.

qualityAttributes.name: Atomicity
qualityAttributes.definition: In databases, the assurance that transactions are treated as single units that either fully succeed or fail.

qualityAttributes.name: Auditability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software logs actions and allows authorized inspection of these logs.

qualityAttributes.name: Autonomy
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which service-oriented software operates independently from its execution environment.

qualityAttributes.name: Availability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software is ready and available for use.

qualityAttributes.name: Capabilities
qualityAttributes.definition: The range of actions, tasks, or functions that the software can perform.

qualityAttributes.name: Compatibility
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software can work effectively with other systems or software.

qualityAttributes.name: Complexity
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree of difficulty to understand, modify, or maintain the software.

qualityAttributes.name: Composability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software's components can be assembled and reassembled.

qualityAttributes.name: Confidentiality
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software protects sensitive information from unauthorized access.

qualityAttributes.name: Configurability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which settings and features within the software can be customized by the user.

qualityAttributes.name: Consistency
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software behaves and presents itself uniformly across different scenarios.

qualityAttributes.name: Correctness
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software performs its functions without error.

qualityAttributes.name: Credibility
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software is reliable and induces trust.

qualityAttributes.name: Customizability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software allows the user to tailor features to their specific needs.

qualityAttributes.name: Debuggability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which bugs can be discovered and fixed within the software.

qualityAttributes.name: Degradability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software can gracefully reduce its functionality in the face of system constraints.

qualityAttributes.name: Demonstrability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software's functions and capabilities can be demonstrated to others.

qualityAttributes.name: Dependability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software can be relied upon to perform its functions accurately and consistently.

qualityAttributes.name: Deployability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software can be easily installed, configured, and put into operation.

qualityAttributes.name: Determinability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software's behavior can be predictably determined from its inputs and conditions.

qualityAttributes.name: Discoverability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software's features and functionalities are easily discoverable by users.

qualityAttributes.name: Distributability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software can be distributed across multiple platforms and environments.

qualityAttributes.name: Durability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software can endure stress and continue to function over extended periods of time.

qualityAttributes.name: Effectiveness
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to achieve its goals and produce desired outcomes.

qualityAttributes.name: Efficiency
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software performs its functions without wasting resources.

qualityAttributes.name: Evolvability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software can adapt to future changes in its environment or requirements.

qualityAttributes.name: Extensibility
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which new features or functionalities can be added to the existing software.

qualityAttributes.name: Failure Transparency
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software reveals or conceals its failures and the impact of those failures.

qualityAttributes.name: Fault-Tolerance
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software continues to function in the presence of errors or failures.

qualityAttributes.name: Fidelity
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software accurately represents or simulates real-world conditions or data.

qualityAttributes.name: Flexibility
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can adapt to different tasks or scenarios.

qualityAttributes.name: Functionality
qualityAttributes.definition: The range and capabilities of tasks that the software can perform.

qualityAttributes.name: Inspectability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software’s internal workings can be examined for debugging or analysis.

qualityAttributes.name: Installability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can be installed and set up for use.

qualityAttributes.name: Integrity
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software prevents unauthorized access and maintains the accuracy of data.

qualityAttributes.name: Interchangeability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which components within the software can be exchanged.

qualityAttributes.name: Interoperability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software can interact with other systems or software components.

qualityAttributes.name: Learnability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which new users can understand and use the software.

qualityAttributes.name: Localizability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to be adapted for different languages, regions, and cultures.

qualityAttributes.name: Maintainability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can be modified, updated, or corrected.

qualityAttributes.name: Manageability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software can be efficiently managed and monitored.

qualityAttributes.name: Mobility
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to operate effectively on different devices or environments.

qualityAttributes.name: Modifiability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software can be easily changed to add new features or fix issues.

qualityAttributes.name: Modularity
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software is composed of independent, interchangeable modules.

qualityAttributes.name: Observability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which internal states of the software can be observed through outputs.

qualityAttributes.name: Operability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can be kept in a functioning state.

qualityAttributes.name: Orthogonality
qualityAttributes.definition: The independence between different features or components of the software.

qualityAttributes.name: Performance
qualityAttributes.definition: The effectiveness of the software in terms of speed, efficiency, and resource usage.

qualityAttributes.name: Portability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can be moved from one environment to another.

qualityAttributes.name: Precision
qualityAttributes.definition: The accuracy with which the software performs its calculations or processes.

qualityAttributes.name: Predictability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software's behavior can be anticipated.

qualityAttributes.name: Privacy
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software ensures that unauthorized users cannot access, modify, or delete personal information.

qualityAttributes.name: Producibility
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can be reliably reproduced or replicated.

qualityAttributes.name: Provability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which formal methods can be used to prove the software's correctness.

qualityAttributes.name: Recoverability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to restore its state and functionality after failure.

qualityAttributes.name: Relevance
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software meets the real-world needs of its users.

qualityAttributes.name: Reliability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to function correctly and consistently.

qualityAttributes.name: Repeatability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software provides the same output for the same input under the same conditions.

qualityAttributes.name: Reproducibility
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability to get the same results consistently across different environments and conditions.

qualityAttributes.name: Resilience
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to adapt and recover from adversity.

qualityAttributes.name: Responsiveness
qualityAttributes.definition: The software's ability to quickly respond to user input or system events.

qualityAttributes.name: Reusability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which components of the software can be used in different contexts.

qualityAttributes.name: Robustness
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to cope with errors and unexpected conditions.

qualityAttributes.name: Safety
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software avoids causing harm to users or the environment.

qualityAttributes.name: Scalability
qualityAttributes.definition: The software's ability to handle increased loads efficiently.

qualityAttributes.name: Seamlessness
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software integrates its various components without visible gaps or inconsistencies.

qualityAttributes.name: Securability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to protect against unauthorized access and data breaches.

qualityAttributes.name: Self-Sustainability
qualityAttributes.definition: The software's ability to maintain its operational state without external intervention.

qualityAttributes.name: Serviceability/Supportability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can be serviced, maintained, and supported.

qualityAttributes.name: Simplicity
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software is easy to understand and use.

qualityAttributes.name: Stability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software remains reliable under different conditions.

qualityAttributes.name: Standards Compliance
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software adheres to industry or regulatory standards.

qualityAttributes.name: Survivability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to endure and recover from catastrophic failures.

qualityAttributes.name: Sustainability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability of the software to endure over time while meeting environmental and social requirements.

qualityAttributes.name: Tailorability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which the software can be customized to meet specific user needs.

qualityAttributes.name: Testability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software can be effectively tested to ensure it meets its requirements.

qualityAttributes.name: Timeliness
qualityAttributes.definition: The software's ability to perform tasks or provide responses within an acceptable time frame.

qualityAttributes.name: Traceability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ability to track changes, data flow, or user actions throughout the software.

qualityAttributes.name: Transparency
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software's actions and decision-making processes are visible to the user.

qualityAttributes.name: Ubiquity
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software is available and functional across various platforms and devices.

qualityAttributes.name: Understandability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which users can comprehend the software's functions and use.

qualityAttributes.name: Upgradability
qualityAttributes.definition: The ease with which new features can be added or existing features can be modified.

qualityAttributes.name: Usability
qualityAttributes.definition: The degree to which the software is easy to use and provides a good user experience.

qualityAttributes.name: Vulnerability
qualityAttributes.definition: The extent to which the software is susceptible to unauthorized access or exploitation.
